summary: Built a Confluence page-creation flow into a reusable skill (my-workflows/xm-ny-weekly-planning.md), then escalated to a persistent macOS LaunchAgent that runs weekly (Monday 10:00) without any chat session open. Discovered and fixed a real bug during testing: the cached OAuth token's granular scopes only authorize Confluence REST API v2, not the legacy v1 content endpoint used elsewhere in the vault's skills.
questions: Should other skills that call Confluence v1 REST endpoints (create-jira-ticket.md's Confluence references, sync-ticket-to-confluence.md) be checked for the same v1-vs-v2 OAuth scope mismatch?
learned: Atlassian OAuth apps granted granular scopes like write:page:confluence / write:comment:confluence only authorize Confluence REST API v2 (/wiki/api/v2/...), not the legacy v1 (/wiki/rest/api/content) — v1 calls fail with 401 'scope does not match' even though the scope list looks sufficient.
v2 API needs a numeric spaceId (resolved via GET /wiki/api/v2/spaces?keys=RT -> 3185017363), not the space key.
v2 footer comments use POST /wiki/api/v2/footer-comments with {pageId, body}, distinct from the v1 content-with-container-type-comment pattern.

confluence_add_comment (MCP tool) accepts raw Confluence storage-format XHTML in its 'body' param despite being documented as Markdown-only -- <ac:link><ri:user ri:account-id=.../></ac:link> renders as a real working @mention; plain markdown '@name' or '[~accountId]' does not.
thinking: Chose to dry-run the full create+comment+delete cycle against the real Confluence space (with an obviously-labeled test title) before trusting the script to run unattended -- caught the v1/v2 scope bug this way instead of discovering it silently next Monday.

Kept the LaunchAgent minimal (no extra notification layer) per Bonnie's explicit choice, but did add local logging (run.log) since that costs nothing and is standard practice for unattended cron/launchd scripts.
followups: Watch the first real Monday run (~2026-07-27 10:00) via ~/.xm-ny-weekly-planning/run.log to confirm the unattended path works end to end.
Consider auditing other skills for the same v1-API OAuth-scope issue found here.
